clue.text: Remains of priest accepted by Roman Catholics

indicators.note: something accepted by a group is taken into it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RC is the standard abbreviation for Roman Catholic, made plural
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: The bones of a dead priest are kept and venerated by the Catholic faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: The priest is the biblical Eli, Samuel's teacher, a crossword favourite. 'Remains of priest' reads as one phrase, but 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are things surviving from the past, so the word serves as a plural noun for leftovers or remnants.

clue.text: Disown, but help to rise in public esteem

indicators.note: the help is placed inside the esteem

parts.note: repute is one's standing in the public eye

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upward, so the letters for help run backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A paradox: rejecting someone while helping them rise in public estimation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help to rise' reads as a single phrase meaning promote, but 'help' gives the letters and 'to rise' turns them upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to refuse to acknowledge or to reject, the same as disowning a person or claim.

clue.text: Assumed name, with no initial, so must be rocky type

definitions.note: an adjective used here as a description of a kind of rock

indicators.note: having no initial means losing the opening letter of the word

parts.note: an alias is a false name someone goes by
sic is Latin for thus or so, used to flag a quotation as written

explanation.surface: A detective reasons that someone with a nameless alias must be a hard sort.
explanation.walkthrough: ALIAS drops its first letter to give LIAS. The Lias is a series of Lower Jurassic rocks in England; Liassic describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Liassic is the geologists' adjective for strata of the Lias, early Jurassic limestones and shales, so it names a kind of rock.

clue.text: Instrument displacing a choir with 655 members?

indicators.note: displacing moves things out of their places, so the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
655 in Roman numerals: D 500, C 100, L 50, V 5
surface padding: turns the number into a headcount of singers

explanation.surface: An instrument so loud it pushes aside a huge choir of 655 singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' is surface colour, turning the number into a headcount; the question mark warns that 655 is to be read as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavichord is an early keyboard where brass tangents strike the strings, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Native of Saragossa, perhaps? And Paris, oddly enough

indicators.note: doing something oddly means not in the usual way, so the letters come out in a strange new order

parts.note: eight letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone from a Spanish city, and also Paris, might be the person in question.
explanation.walkthrough: Saragossa (Zaragoza) is a city in Spain; 'perhaps' marks it as one example, since a Spaniard need not come from there.
explanation.definitionFit: Saragossa lies in Spain, so anyone born there is an example of a person from that country.

clue.text: The Church's noted antithesis to mountain air?

definitions.text: The Church's noted antithesis to mountain air?

parts.words: The Church's noted antithesis to mountain air?
parts.note: surface reading: some church-famous opposite of the bracing atmosphere of high peaks
setter's reading: noted means set to music, air is a tune, and the opposite of mountains is flat lowland, so a tune of the lowlands sung in church

explanation.walkthrough: Air is both breeze and tune, and the opposite of mountains is level ground; the church chant's name splits as lowland plus tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied single-line chant of the medieval Christian liturgy, such as Gregorian chant.

clue.text: It's in a shape that tapers to a point, this plant

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the clue states outright that one thing is inside the other

parts.words: shape that tapers to a point
parts.note: a cone narrows from a round base to an apex
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describes a plant whose flower narrows to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe hides the instruction: read It's as 'It is in', placing the word inside the shape, with the shape keeping its article.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a poisonous flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: The same ardent longing to be senior member

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
a yen is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A newcomer harbours the same burning ambition to rise to the top of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving person in a profession or body, its senior figure.

clue.text: In as good health as this too

definitions.meaning: second meaning: placed after as, the word makes a phrase meaning also

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a fill-in: 'as' followed by the answer is a common phrase meaning too.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means healthy, and the phrase 'as' plus this word means also or in addition.

clue.text: Appease part-time soldiers getting back in position

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the soldiers go within the position

parts.note: a position is a place

indicators.note: getting back means returning, so the soldiers' letters are read from the far end

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An officer soothes reservists who are returning to their posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve, hence part-time soldiers; the turned pair lands inside the position between its fourth and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to calm their anger, a direct synonym of pacify or appease.

clue.text: It sticks to the seabed for the most part — extremely velvety for a fish

indicators.note: only most of the thing is wanted, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: what a ship drops to hold fast to the sea floor

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of velvety

explanation.surface: Describes a bottom-dwelling creature that is very smooth to the touch, as if identifying a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the most part' looks like a hedge about how firmly it sticks, but it trims a letter from the word; the second 'for' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The anchovy is a small, strongly flavoured sea fish of the herring family, used salted on pizzas.

clue.text: Punishment for keeping to the rules?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: correction imposed on someone who has misbehaved
second meaning: orderly, controlled behaviour that obeys a code

explanation.surface: Asks whether being penalised is the reward for obeying regulations, a wry irony.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the two halves are not cause and effect but two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both the act of correcting misconduct by penalty and the orderly obedience that training produces.

clue.text: Right to be situated to the north

parts.note: a place lies where it is located
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Claims a privilege to live up in the northern part of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim to hold another's property until a debt is paid, so it is a kind of right.

clue.text: A friend of Mowgli holds up city, causing uproar

indicators.note: in a down clue holding something up means sitting beneath it, so the friend comes after the city

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire
taken as written
Baloo is the bear who befriends Mowgli in Kipling's Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A bear from the jungle stops traffic in a town, causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds up' suggests delaying the city, but in a down entry it means supporting from below.
explanation.definitionFit: Hullabaloo is a noisy commotion or fuss, a lively synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Drink causes surprised cry in local, perhaps

indicators.note: the cry is placed in the middle of the other word
perhaps admits that the word is one possible form, so its letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then shuffled
a typical exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Beer makes someone in the pub gasp with astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British pub, which gives the surface its setting; the cry splits the shuffled pub word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is the general term for intoxicating liquor, so it can stand for drink in the sense of booze.

clue.text: Conspicuous features of the pound and foreign coins

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound
taken as written
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Notable designs found on British and overseas money.
explanation.definitionFit: Landmarks are prominent objects in a landscape that are easily seen and used to find one's way.

clue.text: Abundant work, you say, and fast?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: you say tells us to take the spoken sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: the letter name sounds the same as the pronoun
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Wonders whether lavish output and abstinence can go together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for speed, but it is the noun for going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means rich and plentiful, lavishly supplied, so it works as a synonym of profuse or ample.

clue.text: Possibly the present Head is causing strain

parts.note: the present is one grammatical tense, among others
a ness is a headland, as in Sheerness or Orford Ness

explanation.surface: The current headteacher is a source of stress in the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a school head, but it is a promontory; ness appears in place names such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenseness is the state of being taut or anxious, which is what strain means as a noun.

clue.text: Stand round printing unit with girl and boy …

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure, half an em
Vi is short for Violet
a common boy's name

explanation.surface: A young pair gather by a printing press, trailing off to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, where girl and boy appear again with different names.
explanation.definitionFit: To environ is an old verb meaning to surround or encircle, as in the related noun environs.

clue.text: It runs outside in the open, and has a woman around

definitions.text: It runs outside in the open

indicators.note: the woman goes around, wrapping the other word inside her

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that dashes about outdoors has a female companion with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and has' reads as a link, but the second 'and' supplies letters and 'has' signals holding them.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform running along the outside of a house, open at the front.

clue.text: … girl and boy building a ship

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a boy's name

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the young couple construct a vessel together.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis picks up the previous clue, where girl and boy gave VI and RON; here they give different names.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked sailing vessel used for war and trade from the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Adopt a couple? Give me a rise first

indicators.note: first places this piece at the front, before the couple
in a down clue raising a word means reading it upward, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a brace is a pair, especially of game birds

explanation.surface: Someone taking in two children asks for a pay increase before doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the reversed ME goes before the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or cause is to take it up willingly, as one adopts a policy.

clue.text: Shelter discovered in Tenby recently

indicators.note: something discovered in a place was lying inside it all along, here inside the following words

parts.note: sits across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A refuge has just been found in a Welsh seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenby is a resort town in Pembrokeshire, Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, a farm building that gives cattle cover from the weather.

clue.text: Support bachelor in present state

indicators.note: the bachelor is put inside the phrase for the state of things

parts.note: as is means in its current condition
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: Backing an unmarried man in the condition he is now in.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes in front of AS IS, which counts as inside when the letters are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or underlying support on which something rests.

clue.text: Claiming to be professional bowled with skill — unbelievable!

parts.note: someone claiming to be something says I'm
short for professional
b is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
able means skilful

explanation.surface: A cricketer boasts of professional status, bowled with flair, and someone exclaims at the boast.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M arrives without its apostrophe, as crosswords ignore punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Improbable means unlikely to be true, close in sense to hard to credit or unbelievable.

clue.text: Many leave detachment afloat on this transporter

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a draft is a party of soldiers detached for a duty
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A crowd of soldiers leaves their unit and floats away on a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Many as D (500) is a crossword convention; D leaves DRAFT. 'Many' wants to be the definition, since a raft of things is many.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating platform of logs or planks used to carry people or goods across water.

clue.text: Boss we may trample underfoot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or ornamental ... on a surface
second meaning: a road marker set into the surface that we walk over

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' wants to be the employer we trample on, but it is a raised knob; the second half is a marker set in a road or path.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a projecting knob or boss on a surface, and also a metal marker set into a road or crossing.

clue.text: 4, perhaps, takes in a Turkish leader as legislator

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it inside, so the outer word wraps round the rest

parts.note: the answer to 4 across is a man from Spain, addressed as señor
taken as written

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: first letter of Turkish

explanation.surface: A Spanish man welcomes a Turkish chief in his role as a lawmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Señor is Spanish for Mr, and crosswords drop its accent. 'Turkish leader' looks like a sultan but means only the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an upper house that makes laws, so the word names a lawmaker.

clue.text: Leaves assembly of agile characters

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together into something new, so these letters are built into another order
characters means letters, telling us it is the letters themselves that are reassembled, not the words

parts.note: seven characters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a gathering of nimble people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb but is the plural noun; 'characters' tells you it is the letters of the two words that are reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is the collective word for the leaves of a plant or tree, so it stands for the plural noun.

clue.text: Careless to strike the instrument panel

parts.note: to slap is to strike with an open hand
short for dashboard, the panel of dials in a car

explanation.surface: It would be reckless to thump the dashboard of the car while driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done hastily and without care, so it is a synonym of sloppy or careless.

clue.text: A great many — with extra for a baker

definitions.meaning: second meaning: sets of twelve, which for a baker run to thirteen

explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen, one more than the usual twelve, from the old practice of adding a loaf to guard against short weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a set of twelve is used loosely for a large but unspecified number, as in lots or heaps.
